request.tone: quiet, aching radio mystery about grief and listening; present tense, rain and static, an ending that hinges on telling the truth
request.note: Catalog book authored by hand; there is no request text. Band, length and style are copied from the book metadata; tone is the plan author's reading.

pitch.hero: Wren Callahan, a girl who cannot sleep and keeps switching on her late grandfather's shortwave
pitch.want: to find out who is sending the numbers loop and why
pitch.obstacle: a station everyone says is dead, a code, a stubborn old man who has stopped hoping, and a deadline she only discovers late
pitch.stake: at twenty to midnight the relay's dying cell will play an old man's last goodbye to a daughter who may not be listening, and erase thirty years of tape
pitch.ending_kind: success: father and daughter reconnected, or the channel and its tapes saved for later

wren.name: Wren Callahan
wren.want: to answer the question the loop keeps asking, and the one her grandfather left unfinished
wren.voice: careful, honest, grieving; logs things the way he taught her; brave in a frightened, deliberate way

kell.name: Kell Alder
kell.role: operator of Relay KX, alone for thirty years
kell.want: to keep the channel open for his daughter, and now to say goodbye and let her be
kell.voice: old, gruff, plain-spoken, closed until met with plain truth ("Tonight I am only saying goodbye")

marin.name: Marin Alder
marin.want: unspoken: to be asked home without being pushed
marin.voice: heard as a girl's careful voice reading numbers, and at the end as a woman's

okafor.name: Mrs. Okafor
okafor.want: for someone to finally listen to Kell, and to be told the truth before she helps
okafor.voice: sharp as fishhooks, few words, kind under it

grandpa.name: Wren's grandfather (Callahan)
grandpa.want: that somebody answer the poor man on the headland
grandpa.voice: square capitals, cramped logbooks, unposted letters

truth.statement: When the county shut Relay KX thirty years ago, its senior operator Kell Alder refused to leave. His daughter Marin had gone after a quarrel, and every night since he has broadcast a loop of her girlhood voice reading the station numbers, with a gap to listen for her answer. The station's power cell is failing, and tonight at twenty to midnight it will play his last recorded goodbye and erase itself. Wren's grandfather heard him for years, answered in two dots Kell never understood, and wrote him letters he never posted.

loop_nightly.text: For a week Wren has heard a loop on her late grandfather's shortwave: a young woman's careful voice reading numbers, then a falling tone, then the cycle restarts.

grandpa_dead_year.text: Wren's grandfather, a radio operator, died about a year ago, and only she still comes up to his attic.

battery_on_shelf.text: His spare battery, wrapped in a rag and labelled JUST IN CASE, sits on the attic shelf.

headset_on_hook.text: His heavy operator's headset hangs on a hook; he swore it let you hear the room behind a voice.

has_battery.text: Wren has his spare battery in the bottom of her pack.

grandpa_logbook.text: Her grandfather logged everything he heard on that radio for forty years.

relay_dark.text: The relay station on the headland has stood dark for as long as Wren can remember.

loop_from_relay.text: The loop comes from the old relay station on the headland.

notice_card.text: A fresh card on the pier board gives the loop's frequency and says "if you hear the loop, it is real."

relay_alive.text: The relay is not dead: it is tended, powered, and one window is lit.

alder_name.text: The man keeping the relay running is named Alder.

log_no_answer.text: The relay's log board ends in forty lines of LOOP HOLDING, STILL NO ANSWER.

for_m.text: The newest log page ends FOR M, STILL HOLDING.

loop_promise.text: A note in the relay cellar: LOOP STAYS UP WHILE I DRAW BREATH, KX.

grandpa_tracked_alder.text: Her grandfather followed the KX loop for years and wanted somebody to answer Alder, but never told anyone.

grandpa_wrote_kell.text: Her grandfather wrote years of unposted letters to Kell at Relay KX.

alder_has_daughter.text: Kell Alder has a daughter, gone after a quarrel, whom he has never given up on.

kell_alder_30y.text: The operator is Kell Alder of Station KX, alone at his desk every night for thirty years.

left_note.text: Wren wedged a note, I HEAR YOU and a W, in Kell Alder's door frame.

station_decommissioned.text: Officially the relay was decommissioned thirty years ago and has no staff.

message_for_m.text: Decoded, the numbers say STILL HOLDING THE CHANNEL OPEN FOR M.

count_going_down.text: Part of the loop is a count, and it is running down.

ends_tonight.text: The count reaches zero tonight, at twenty to midnight.

alder_refused_transfer.text: Kell Alder alone refused the transfer inland when the relay closed: "somebody has to keep the channel open."

okafor_trust.text: Wren told Mrs. Okafor the truth; she told Wren of the daughter and asked her to ring the marina if the loop looked like stopping.

okafor_pins_card.text: Mrs. Okafor has pinned a card to the pier board every month for thirty years saying the loop is real.

m_in_morse.text: The two long tones that start each cycle are Morse for M.

gap_listening.text: After each cycle there is a four-second gap: the sender stops and listens for an answer.

voice_is_daughter.text: The voice reading the numbers is Kell Alder's daughter Marin, recorded at seventeen.

m_is_marin.text: M is Marin, Kell Alder's daughter.

spring_tide_tonight.text: A spring tide with a gale behind it will top out at the relay at about twenty to midnight.

cell_dying.text: The relay's only power cell is long past its life and will fail tonight.

final_tape_erase.text: At zero the station will play a final tape once, then erase all its tapes.

alder_thanks_w.text: Kell Alder recorded a thank-you to "the W who left three words in my door."

gale_tonight.text: A gale is blowing on the headland tonight.

circled_number.text: In Kell Alder's address book one telephone number is circled until the paper shines.

hold_switch.text: A guarded HOLD switch on the console would stop both the sending and the erasing.

second_terminals.text: Beside the dying cell are bare terminals for a second cell that was never fitted.

station_register.text: Tucked inside the back cover of her grandfather's logbook is the club's printed station register, the one book every operator on this coast once owned.

n_open.event: Sleepless, Wren switches on her late grandfather's shortwave and hears the numbers loop again, read in a young woman's careful voice.

n_shelf.event: His spare battery (JUST IN CASE) and his operator's headset: she lets herself take down one thing.

n_shelf_battery.event: The cold battery goes into the bottom of her pack.

n_shelf_headset.event: Through his headset the loop opens into a big dark room.

n_start.event: Coordinates, the dark relay on the headland, or the logbook he kept for forty years.

r_coord_1.event: Plotted, two pairs fall on the harbour and the ridge water tower.

r_coord_harbor.event: At the harbour: the harbourmaster's lit hut, the tide-gauge shed, the notice-board.

r_coord_notice.event: A fresh card: the loop's frequency and "if you hear the loop, it is real."

r_coord_notice2.event: The card's ink is still damp; was it meant for her?

r_coord_notice3.event: Tuned to the card's frequency, the signal swells toward the headland.

e_coord_notice.event: She leaves the card; it blows away and is replaced; the loop ends while she waits.

r_coord_harbor_ask.event: Mr. Pell: the loop used to come off the old headland relay, kept going by somebody stubborn.

r_coord_harbor_shed.event: A "dead" shed with a live receiver blinking to the loop; force the door or copy the frequency.

r_coord_shed_in.event: The receiver is only an ear for RELAY KX, kept working for years.

e_coord_shed_leave.event: At home the frequency is already pencil-ticked on Grandpa's dial; by the weekend it is only hiss.

r_coord_tower.event: At the water tower the signal is strongest: a cageless ladder, or the service box.

r_coord_climb.event: Frozen on the ladder, Wren sees a cable running from the antenna to the relay.

r_coord_base.event: A rusted service box, and stencilled arrows along the ridge.

r_coord_base_in.event: A tag: KX RELAY, HEADLAND, DO NOT DISCONNECT; the tower is only a repeater.

r_coord_base_out.event: Nineteen reflective arrows lead along the ridge toward the headland.

r_coord_beat.event: Along the headland track the loop grows clean: the numbers point to the relay on the point.

r_coord_close.event: From the overlook the relay is lit; Wren creeps to the window.

r_relay_1.event: At the dark relay's chained gate: an open cliff path or a flooded sheltered lane.

r_re_path.event: The wind-blown cliff path, a gap in the fence, and the mast close enough to photograph.

r_re_gap.event: Inside the fence: RELAY KX, cut weeds, new cable, a running generator.

e_re_photo.event: She photographs the mast and goes home; one blurred photo shows a man with a mug; the loop stops the very next night, before she returns.

r_re_lane.event: The lane: a lit gatehouse log board, a humming transformer hut, a flooding cellar.

r_re_cellar.event: Water rising in the cellar; a sleeved note whose first word is LOOP.

r_re_cellar2.event: LOOP STAYS UP WHILE I DRAW BREATH, KX, and the water rising.

r_re_cellar3.event: Wren saves the note and is nearly swept down by the surge.

e_re_cellar.event: She escapes the cellar with the words read; fever keeps her in bed until the loop is gone.

r_re_gatehouse.event: A warm gatehouse with a years-long log board; a dog barks nearby.

r_re_log.event: LOOP HOLDING, STILL NO ANSWER, forty lines deep; a man with a dog passes the door.

r_re_scrap.event: The stolen page: FOR M, STILL HOLDING.

r_re_hut.event: SERVICED BY K. ALDER, last month and every month for years.

r_relay_beat.event: In the rain, one lit window and a swept step under the mast: the voice comes from in there.

r_relay_close.event: A cabin, not a station, with boots on the step.

r_notes_1.event: Where would he have logged it: the cedar trunk or the radio shed?

r_no_trunk.event: The trunk: a water-stained logbook, QSL cards, and unstamped letters.

r_no_letters.event: Unstamped letters to Relay KX, to "Kell": "she may still be out there, so keep the channel open."

r_no_letters2.event: The letter names Kell Alder and pleads with him not to give up on his own daughter.

r_no_letters3.event: More unposted letters tell Kell that somebody hears him and his girl may be listening.

e_no_letters.event: Leaving the letters unread, she later finds his note to carry them to KX; there is only hiss.

r_no_book.event: Grandpa's logbook: ALDER STILL TRANSMITTING, WHY; his last page asks whether anybody will answer the poor man.

r_no_cards.event: A heavier QSL card names KX ALDER.

r_no_freq.event: Three cards name RELAY KX and Alder, matching the loop; four figures of nights, and nobody ever answered.

e_no_cards_end.event: Sorting until three, Wren finds an eleven-year-old card: "Heard KX again tonight, please do not tell him, M."

r_no_shed.event: The shed: walls of tuning notes and a padlocked cabinet.

r_no_tuning.event: A twice-circled note: KX LOOP, HEADLAND RELAY, OPERATOR ALDER, DO NOT GIVE UP ON HIM.

e_no_locked.event: The cabinet falls; a card behind it says KX, EVERY MIDNIGHT, TWO DOTS, NO REPLY YET.

r_notes_beat.event: Grandpa knew someone named Alder kept the headland station alive and never told a soul.

r_notes_close.event: Through the fence to the lit window of the relay.

n_b1.event: Through the window: Kell Alder of Station KX, thirty years of logbooks, a steaming mug; a flashlight comes.

n_b1_note.event: Wren wedges I HEAR YOU, W in his door and runs; the flashlight stops at the door.

n_b1_slip.event: Wren slips away unseen; he never knew she was there.

n_b1_echo.event: At home, the county says KX was decommissioned thirty years ago with no staff.

n_b1_choice.event: Crack the numbers he sends every night, or ask the town about him.

m_numbers_1.event: A book cipher keyed to the station register tucked in Grandpa's logbook, or timing the groups.

m_num_cipher.event: Against the station register, HOLDING, ANSWER and M appear; one cluster refuses.

m_num_cracked.event: The register key holds: STILL HOLDING THE CHANNEL OPEN FOR M; the final figure is a count going down.

m_num_book2.event: The tide table yields one date and hour and nothing else.

m_num_cracked2.event: The trusted fragment: today, 23:40; a clock set for tonight.

e_num_gibberish.event: Running the tide table over everything until one in the morning, she misses the end; 23:40 was the whole message.

m_num_time.event: The gaps between cycles are shrinking.

m_num_intervals.event: The curve of the shrinking gaps hits zero tonight, a little before midnight.

m_num_pattern.event: The rough figures land on today; trust it or test it.

e_num_giveup.event: Static gives a date too, so she gives up; at twenty to midnight a man says one name and the loop is gone.

m_who_1.event: The library microfilm, or Mrs. Okafor at the marina.

m_who_film.event: A photo of the relay's closing, and one man apart.

m_who_article.event: Kell Alder alone refused the transfer: "somebody has to keep the channel open."

m_who_photo.event: "K. Alder, the one who would not go," and a neighbour's letter that nobody is listening.

m_who_okafor.event: Mrs. Okafor wants to know why Wren asks about Alder before she says a word.

m_who_story.event: Told the truth, Okafor tells of Kell's daughter, their quarrel and his vow, and her monthly pier card; ring the marina if it stops.

e_who_warn.event: Not for a school project: Okafor sends her home with a question, why would a man keep a girl's voice on the air for thirty years?

n_b2.event: The two long tones are Morse M; after the count comes a four-second gap: he is waiting for an answer.

n_b2_under.event: Under the voice through his headset, an old recording: the numbers girl, not much older than Wren, answering "Dad."

n_b2_echo.event: Logged night by night, the tone starts lower and the gap shrinks: the loop is running out.

n_b2_choice.event: Two questions: who is M, and what does the count run down to?

mm_listener_1.event: The loop gives only a letter: M could be a person in the records or a place on Grandpa's chart.

mm_list_family.event: Records: Kell's one child, Marin, vanished thirty years ago; his sister still lives by the harbour.

mm_list_daughter.event: A forum: Kell's girl read the station numbers, then left; M is Marin and the loop an apology.

mm_list_sister.event: His sister: M is Marin, his girl; one terrible quarrel; an address two ridges west.

mm_list_place.event: A twice-ringed M by a mooring on Grandpa's chart.

mm_list_map.event: The buoy's plate: Marin, HER MOORING IS KEPT.

e_list_deadend.event: Working through every chart mark, she hears the loop end on a name.

mm_count_1.event: Follow the falling line, or check this year's tide table and the forecast.

mm_count_time.event: The line hits zero at twenty to midnight; a maintenance sheet and a schedule to read.

mm_count_extrap.event: The relay's single cell is eleven years past its life; its decay meets her line at the same minute.

mm_count_clock.event: The schedule's FINAL line: PLAY TAPE 2, THEN ERASE ALL, today at twenty to midnight.

mm_count_tide.event: Tonight's spring tide tops out at eighteen to midnight, with a gale warning; she knows what a spring tide does to the low road under the headland.

mm_count_warn.event: Trusting the tide, the station will drown as the count hits zero.

e_count_wait.event: Waiting for daylight, she wakes to the news that the tide knocked out the old relay.

n_b3.event: At 22:40 a recorded voice: "this is your father, Marin"; the cell has one hour; then the loop resumes, no longer restarting.

n_b3_note.event: In the gap, a new recording: thanks to "the W who left three words in my door."

n_b3_echo.event: A gale hits; one hour is nothing; he will spend it talking to someone who left.

n_b3_choice.event: Fifty-nine minutes, an old man beside a failing cell, a daughter who may not be listening: ride out, use Grandpa's transmitter, or telephone someone.

f_station_1.event: At the flooded relay with nine minutes: climb the fence or take the service road.

f_st_fence.event: In the yard: run thirty open yards in the gale, or creep round the sheds.

f_st_control.event: The empty control room: the countdown, AFTER LAST SEND, ERASE, a HOLD switch, a circled number, a guttering cell.

f_st_answer.event: Dial the circled number so his message reaches her, or throw HOLD and save the tapes.

e_st_reunite.event: Dialled through, his goodbye reaches Marin's kitchen; Wren hands him the phone.

e_st_archive.event: HOLD at eleven seconds: nothing sent, nothing erased; he decides to stay.

f_st_power.event: The cell is failing; bare terminals for a second cell.

f_st_spliced.event: JUST IN CASE: Grandpa's battery holds the station for hours.

e_st_stabilize.event: The radio club brings trucks; HOLD is thrown and Marin is called.

e_st_both.event: HOLD, then the circled number: Marin hears her father's tape as he walks in.

e_st_record.event: Nursing the cell gets one word, "Marin," onto the phone she set recording in the yard, before it dies; the spare battery was the case.

e_st_hesitate.event: Going round the sheds, she arrives one minute late to an erased station and a circled number.

f_st_road.event: Through the back window, Alder hunched in his headset; the door is bolted.

f_st_alder.event: Kell Alder lets her in: he believes Marin is not listening; tonight he is only saying goodbye.

e_st_alder_send.event: Admitting she cannot promise, Wren persuades Kell to speak live; Marin answers "Dad?"

e_st_alder_refuse.event: A promise he knows nobody can make closes him; the tape plays and erases.

e_st_note.event: The note was hers; he learns her grandfather sent two dots every midnight; live, he calls Marin and she answers.

e_st_wait.event: Hammering unheard at the steel door, she hears his goodbye in the voice from the tape an hour ago: "Marin, I kept your voice on the air."

f_relay_1.event: Grandpa's transmitter: send it herself, or ring the radio net's emergency line.

f_re_rig.event: Patching the loop through with her voice for Marin; his pencil mark or the red band.

f_re_boost.event: At the pencil mark, calling Marin; a silent carrier answers, and the phone rings downstairs.

e_re_answer.event: Wren speaks to the carrier; Marin answers in the numbers voice grown older, which settles whose voice the loop kept, and hears her father "kept her voice on a loop."

e_re_neighbor.event: A neighbour's brother, the net controller, carries the message down the coast.

e_re_fuse.event: Ten seconds in the red band, then blue smoke; a neighbour heard and wants the rest.

f_re_club.event: The net's recording: press one for danger, or leave a message for six tomorrow.

f_re_net.event: The duty controller puts the call across the county; a woman two ridges west asks what it says.

e_re_found.event: Patched through, Marin says she read those numbers at seventeen; her father answers live.

e_re_log.event: Twenty-three stations promise to keep calling Marin.

e_re_message.event: Her message is heard at six; Marin has asked after KX every winter for eleven years.

f_help_1.event: Whom to wake: the coast guard auxiliary, a relay man from Grandpa's book, or Mrs. Okafor.

f_he_okafor.event: Okafor knows at once it is stopping, drives her out and opens the back door with Kell's key.

e_he_okafor.event: Okafor makes Kell dial the circled number; Marin answers.

f_he_cg.event: The duty officer wants location and emergency; she has that careful voice counting and an old man.

f_he_act.event: She gives place, hazard and hour; the officer works out the spring tide himself ("Occupied building, headland, spring tide plus gale"), and the crew reaches Alder with hands for one job.

e_he_escort.event: The clerk finds Marin's number and the chief puts her through to her father.

e_he_safe.event: Sandbags, a generator, HOLD at four seconds; a missing-relative file for Marin; "how did a schoolgirl know to give the place, the danger and the hour first?"

e_he_dismiss.event: The whole story goes under curiosities; the sea floods the relay and the tapes.

f_he_colleague.event: Grandpa's book: eight relay men transferred inland, and Ruiz, who STAYED, WON'T TALK.

f_he_join.event: Ruiz drives her out: thirty years of two old men not talking; stay in the truck?

e_he_complete.event: It takes all three: Ruiz wires a spare cell, Kell holds the count, and Wren dials the circled number; Marin answers.

e_he_takeover.event: Waiting in the truck, she never learns whether Marin answered.

e_he_dead.event: The inland men point to Ruiz, too late: the lamp went out eleven minutes ago.

payoff_sites.shows: Grandpa's JUST IN CASE battery holds the station for hours
without it she saves one word before the cell dies
through his headset she hears the girl on the old tape call the operator "Dad"
without it she hears only the gap
Kell has recorded a thank-you to the W who left the note
she tells him the note was hers, and he learns her grandfather was answering him
Okafor drives her out, lets her in with Kell's key, and makes him dial
